reviews.title: Works with obs/streamlabs
reviews.comment: Great quality true 4k and 60fps. Good for streaming, connects to obs/streamlabs just fine and  the software for it is immaculate. If you want the best picture quality, buy a soft box light. Just one is good enough and it can be a cheap one, I got one for $30lol and it works very well. Built in mic is garbage don’t use it.
reviews.author: Sebastian

reviews.title: Studio-Quality Video for Podcasts and Zoom Calls Without the Fuss
reviews.comment: This webcam has been an absolute game-changer for both my podcast recordings and daily Zoom calls. The 4K image quality is incredibly sharp and professional, and the larger 1/2" sensor really makes a difference in low light, my video looks clean and natural without needing a bunch of extra lighting. Setup was quick and painless, and it works flawlessly with my PC and recording software. What impressed me most is how polished everything looks on camera. Whether I’m recording a podcast episode or joining a meeting, people constantly comment on how clear and high-quality my video is. The autofocus is fast, colors are accurate, and it feels like a huge upgrade from typical webcams. If you want broadcast-level quality without the hassle of a full camera setup, this is an outstanding choice. Highly recommended for creators, professionals, and anyone who wants to look their best on video.
reviews.author: Doug Ballinger

reviews.title: A very nice upgrade.
reviews.comment: For years I had a DSLR for my webcam. It suddenly broke out of nowhere. While the DSLR was/is probably still better, the pros of the Meet 2 more than make up for the quality "drop". It's much more cost effective at only ~$100 depending on the sale(s). The footprint is significantly smaller, giving more mounting flexibility and options, and being just plug-and-play makes a world of difference. The quality is still incredible too. The only downside I've noticed is the auto-focus is a little slow. It takes a couple seconds to focus which could be annoying in some scenarios. Regardless, the quality, price, and ease of use is 100% worth it.
reviews.author: LXNDRCTS

reviews.title: Good camera quality, poor mounting stand
reviews.comment: This camera is great for work calls. It provides a quality video and is super small. I did not rate it as 5 stars for 2 reasons. The fact that it requires software to be downloaded on the device you’re using it, which my job does not support and the second is the poor mounting “stand” it comes with - it does not secure the camera on the monitor properly and falls constantly! It’s super annoying and I actually ended up taking the back! I eventually had to buy another stand for it. I do like that it’s magnetic, even though it could be stronger. Overall, I would recommend. It’s a great price, travel friendly size, easy ply-and-play capability, and provides excellent video quality…just be prepared to buy a monitor mount to avoid consistent falling.
reviews.author: Victoria

reviews.title: Finally, a webcam that gets it.
reviews.comment: This is a great webcam. It's got good quality video, it's easy to setup, and most importantly it doesn't hide any settings from you. Tell me, what's easier?... Setting the zoom to hide any clutter you have in your room, or cleaning up the clutter? Setting the white balance, or repainting your room so the camera doesn't get confused? Setting the camera's iso, or setting up studio lights? Most other cameras hide these important settings from you because they don't want to "confuse" you. But what they're really doing is forcing you to adjust -to the camera-. But not the Obsbot Meet, it gives you all the settings you need to adjust the camera -to you-. There are, however, a few minor drawbacks: 1- The camera gets warm, even while in "sleep" mode. This means it's drawing a bit of power. 2- The microphone isn't the best, but it's not the worst either. 3- When I first plugged it in, it took 20 minutes to update the firmware 4- It uses a USB 2 connection. Meaning, all your video will be compressed, and there is an ever so slight delay. Still, it doesn't look bad. 5- I couldn't get the auto-tracking working. It just zoomed out to maximum. When I got it, I thought I'd use the HDR mode, but then didn't. If you don't want to go through careful setup HDR does make it a little easier, but if you play with it a little, you'll get better results without it, meaning the HDR probably isn't the best (but it's not bad). I don't know much about photography, but the interface made it easier enough to figure everything out. I find it a little ironic that OBS is a program most streamers use, called "Open Broadcast Software." It's used crop, tweak, and color correct. But this "OBS"-bot camera includes enough of that on it's own so that you don't have to use OBS. It's smaller than I expected. I'm guessing it's only as big as it needs to be. I like the look of it a lot. Stylish without drawing attention to itself. And the attachable privacy flap is great, since you don't have to worry about losing it.
reviews.author: JP
